gates.name: Proof-of-Concept Verification Gate
gates.criteria: Empirical validation and experimental design: test reproducibility, baseline specification and quantitative success criteria; hypothesis verdicts backed by hypothesis tests, novelty justification, qualitative or interpretability analysis where it applies and a summarized discussion per stage. It passes when a proof of concept closes with a complete discussion and the operator verified its results and contrasted hypotheses (smith novelty approve --gate poc, or the Novelty tab); the full experiments start only after it.

gates.name: Novelty & Findings Gate
gates.criteria: Scientific novelty assessment and empirical evidence support: hypothesis contrast vs SOTA, reviewer defense audit, and explicit operator authorization before manuscript scaffolding and drafting.

gates.name: Writing Readiness Gate
gates.criteria: Section contracts validated with a closed grammar and resolved dependencies.

gates.name: Coupling Verification Gate
gates.criteria: Demanded facts (formulation, design, results) coupled with the authorship and funding declarations.

gates.name: Grounding & Style Leak Gate
gates.criteria: No empty citations or placeholders; strict isolation of bibliographic sources.

gates.name: Diagram & Raster Gate
gates.criteria: Compilation check of TikZ diagrams, methodological schemes and vector figures.

actions.label: Explore the plausibility of the idea
guide: Write the idea in at least two sentences: the problem and what you propose (otherwise the agent refuses to search).
The agent gathers ~25 SOTA references by their abstracts, in 3 to 7 families, and draws the constellation (atlas.html).
Then it splits the hypothesis into claims and grades each one (novel / known / tension / contradicted) with verbatim quotes.
Nothing is ingested or filed: the report awaits your acceptance before the top 5 move on to ingestion.
You can adjust the idea and ask for a new screening; every pass is a new report.
No clear idea yet? Open Thematic help, give 3 to 5 keywords and the Banco LIA proposes one you can edit and approve.

actions.label: Deliberate the experimental design
guide: The question that governs every turn: what experiment would test this claim of the proposal?
Every experiment declares the claim it tests, its metric and its SOTA baseline.
Every experiment is justified by 2 to 5 references of the SOTA pool in .papersmith/citations.json; the implementation stays locked until then.
Ask for the first version, a change or a revision operation; nothing is applied without your approval.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: design the experiment that tests claim C1 against the strongest SOTA baseline.

actions.label: Data: always a toy set, plus the official dataset
guide: Verbs: synth (a seeded toy set, always), search, license, qc, prepare and publish.
dataset-scout searches the paper's official repositories, Kaggle, Hugging Face, OpenNeuro and Zenodo, and decides the license.
dataset-curator measures the quality (qc) and writes one official subject-wise preparation that the PoC and the experiments read.
publish uploads a private dataset only with your explicit consent; making it public asks for a separate consent.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: synth an 8-subject toy set and look for an official dataset for the task.

actions.label: Replication of comparison methods
guide: The paper-replicator agent replicates every baseline or comparison paper ingested in guidance/.
It stays locked until every experiment of the latest protocol carries its 2 to 5 SOTA citations (G-SOTA-CITATIONS).
It first looks for the paper's published code: when it exists, it adopts it pinned to a commit with its license and audits that it matches the paper and is implemented correctly.
When there is no published code, it reimplements the method from the ingested Markdown; every hyperparameter cites its section or equation.
It ends with REPLICATION.md, invariant tests and a short run on the toy set; it never launches a remote run.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: replicate the guidance/smith-2024 baseline in ../my-poc

actions.label: Implement the proof of concept
guide: Turns the latest proposal into Python against a target repository, or verifies an existing implementation.
It stays locked until every experiment of the latest protocol carries its 2 to 5 SOTA citations (G-SOTA-CITATIONS).
Give the target repository and whether it is a first pass or a later one.

It is done when Results/discussion.json is complete: hypothesis verdicts backed by tests, novelty and qualitative analysis (python skills/_core/results/discussion_cli.py scaffold|check --product <path>).
actions.placeholder: E.g.: implement the PoC of proposal r03 in ../my-poc

actions.label: Estimate the time and choose where to run
actions.desc: Before the pilot and again before the full run: a short timing probe (one epoch of one fold per arm) in Results/timing.json; the Experiments tab estimates the PoC and the full run (±20%), shows the local environment and the local, Kaggle and Colab run options.

actions.label: Hyperparameter search (Optuna)
guide: Only when the deliberation judged it worthwhile: the protocol declares the search and its space.
Nested inside the training subjects of each outer fold, never seeing the test subjects.
The same trial budget for every arm and baseline; it never tunes an independent variable the experiment tests.
A seeded sampler and a declared importance evaluator (Optuna 5 uses PED-ANOVA by default).
report writes the contours and importances the Experiments tab shows.
It runs remotely like the full run, and only the operator launches it.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: plan for the hybrid and linear arms with 40 trials and fANOVA as the evaluator.

actions.label: Implement and measure the experiments
guide: Turns the current experimental protocol into Python and runs its declared measurements.
Give the target repository; the verification compares against the protocol and the proposal.
It is done when Results/discussion.json is complete (python skills/_core/results/discussion_cli.py scaffold|check --product <path>); the full run needs a hypothesis test behind every verdict.
Before any remote rehearsal, experiments-reviewer reviews the code (quality, optimization, GPU use and statistical tests) and hands in its report.
It starts only after the proof of concept is verified (G-EXP-POC): a complete PoC discussion and the operator's approval in the Novelty tab or with smith novelty approve --gate poc.
It also waits for the 2 to 5 SOTA citations of every experiment of the latest protocol (G-SOTA-CITATIONS).
actions.placeholder: E.g.: implement E1 and E2 and report the metrics.

actions.label: Diagrams of the PoC and of the experiments
guide: When the PoC is approved (AGREED.md) it draws the poc diagram; when the full experiments are approved (Experimental_AGREED.md), the experiments diagram.
Each one is a TikZ figure (PDF and PNG) in <product>/diagrams/; the "Generate diagram" button of the Experiments tab also produces it.

Validate it yourself in the Experiments tab ("Validate diagram") or approve it explicitly in the chat with the agent, which runs validate with your words: submit refuses with DIAGRAM_NOT_VALIDATED until then, and drawing it again asks for a new validation.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: poc for the product implementations/my-poc/Model.

actions.label: Decide whether to split across accounts
guide: First estimate --timing <target>/<Name>/Results/timing.json: the range per stage and host (±20%).
Then assess with the measured inputs; --owners is the number of distinct owners in the team (smith team list), never the number of accounts.
Team rule: one account per person and service; each person registers with `smith team add --owner <slug> --name "<name>" --kaggle-username <username> --attest`.
It places, generates and launches nothing: the operator reads the verdict.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: estimate the PoC with its timing.json and assess splitting the full run among 3 owners.

actions.label: Validate the Kaggle accounts
guide: validate re-checks every stored account against the service and takes whatever is in kaggle-inbox/ (kaggle.json or a `username token` line).
Only the accounts the team registry assigns to an owner are workers: one per person.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: validate the accounts and take the new credentials from the inbox.

actions.label: Remote rehearsal and launch (Kaggle / Colab)
guide: Order: generate-job → submit --smoke → fetch --smoke and smoke record → readiness → gate (operator only) → submit → status / poll → fetch.
The ledger is append-only; if the accounts do not authenticate, use /kaggle-accounts first.
Only the operator authorizes a launch: no agent runs submit on its own.
submit (--smoke too) requires that you validated the diagrams of the approved PoC and experiments.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: generate the job for experiments/e1.py and prepare its smoke rehearsal.

actions.label: Explore the plausibility of the idea
guide: Write the idea in at least two sentences: the problem and what you propose (otherwise the agent refuses to search).
The agent gathers ~25 SOTA references by their abstracts, in 3 to 7 families, and draws the constellation (atlas.html).
Then it splits the hypothesis into claims and grades each one (novel / known / tension / contradicted) with verbatim quotes.
Nothing is ingested or filed: the report awaits your acceptance before the top 5 move on to ingestion.
You can adjust the idea and ask for a new screening; every pass is a new report.
No clear idea yet? Open Thematic help, give 3 to 5 keywords and the Banco LIA proposes one you can edit and approve.

actions.label: Deliberate the experimental design
guide: The question that governs every turn: what experiment would test this claim of the proposal?
Every experiment declares the claim it tests, its metric and its SOTA baseline.
Every experiment is justified by 2 to 5 references of the SOTA pool in .papersmith/citations.json; the implementation stays locked until then.
Ask for the first version, a change or a revision operation; nothing is applied without your approval.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: design the experiment that tests claim C1 against the strongest SOTA baseline.

actions.label: Data: always a toy set, plus the official dataset
guide: Verbs: synth (a seeded toy set, always), search, license, qc, prepare and publish.
dataset-scout searches the paper's official repositories, Kaggle, Hugging Face, OpenNeuro and Zenodo, and decides the license.
dataset-curator measures the quality (qc) and writes one official subject-wise preparation that the PoC and the experiments read.
publish uploads a private dataset only with your explicit consent; making it public asks for a separate consent.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: synth an 8-subject toy set and look for an official dataset for the task.

actions.label: Replication of comparison methods
guide: The paper-replicator agent replicates every baseline or comparison paper ingested in guidance/.
It stays locked until every experiment of the latest protocol carries its 2 to 5 SOTA citations (G-SOTA-CITATIONS).
It first looks for the paper's published code: when it exists, it adopts it pinned to a commit with its license and audits that it matches the paper and is implemented correctly.
When there is no published code, it reimplements the method from the ingested Markdown; every hyperparameter cites its section or equation.
It ends with REPLICATION.md, invariant tests and a short run on the toy set; it never launches a remote run.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: replicate the guidance/smith-2024 baseline in ../my-poc

actions.label: Implement the proof of concept
guide: Turns the latest proposal into Python against a target repository, or verifies an existing implementation.
It stays locked until every experiment of the latest protocol carries its 2 to 5 SOTA citations (G-SOTA-CITATIONS).
Give the target repository and whether it is a first pass or a later one.

It is done when Results/discussion.json is complete: hypothesis verdicts backed by tests, novelty and qualitative analysis (python skills/_core/results/discussion_cli.py scaffold|check --product <path>).
actions.placeholder: E.g.: implement the PoC of proposal r03 in ../my-poc

actions.label: Estimate the time and choose where to run
actions.desc: Before the pilot and again before the full run: a short timing probe (one epoch of one fold per arm) in Results/timing.json; the Experiments tab estimates the PoC and the full run (±20%), shows the local environment and the local, Kaggle and Colab run options.

actions.label: Hyperparameter search (Optuna)
guide: Only when the deliberation judged it worthwhile: the protocol declares the search and its space.
Nested inside the training subjects of each outer fold, never seeing the test subjects.
The same trial budget for every arm and baseline; it never tunes an independent variable the experiment tests.
A seeded sampler and a declared importance evaluator (Optuna 5 uses PED-ANOVA by default).
report writes the contours and importances the Experiments tab shows.
It runs remotely like the full run, and only the operator launches it.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: plan for the hybrid and linear arms with 40 trials and fANOVA as the evaluator.

actions.label: Implement and measure the experiments
guide: Turns the current experimental protocol into Python and runs its declared measurements.
Give the target repository; the verification compares against the protocol and the proposal.
It is done when Results/discussion.json is complete (python skills/_core/results/discussion_cli.py scaffold|check --product <path>); the full run needs a hypothesis test behind every verdict.
Before any remote rehearsal, experiments-reviewer reviews the code (quality, optimization, GPU use and statistical tests) and hands in its report.
It starts only after the proof of concept is verified (G-EXP-POC): a complete PoC discussion and the operator's approval in the Novelty tab or with smith novelty approve --gate poc.
It also waits for the 2 to 5 SOTA citations of every experiment of the latest protocol (G-SOTA-CITATIONS).
actions.placeholder: E.g.: implement E1 and E2 and report the metrics.

actions.label: Diagrams of the PoC and of the experiments
guide: When the PoC is approved (AGREED.md) it draws the poc diagram; when the full experiments are approved (Experimental_AGREED.md), the experiments diagram.
Each one is a TikZ figure (PDF and PNG) in <product>/diagrams/; the "Generate diagram" button of the Experiments tab also produces it.

Validate it yourself in the Experiments tab ("Validate diagram") or approve it explicitly in the chat with the agent, which runs validate with your words: submit refuses with DIAGRAM_NOT_VALIDATED until then, and drawing it again asks for a new validation.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: poc for the product implementations/my-poc/Model.

actions.label: Decide whether to split across accounts
guide: First estimate --timing <target>/<Name>/Results/timing.json: the range per stage and host (±20%).
Then assess with the measured inputs; --owners is the number of distinct owners in the team (smith team list), never the number of accounts.
Team rule: one account per person and service; each person registers with `smith team add --owner <slug> --name "<name>" --kaggle-username <username> --attest`.
It places, generates and launches nothing: the operator reads the verdict.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: estimate the PoC with its timing.json and assess splitting the full run among 3 owners.

actions.label: Validate the Kaggle accounts
guide: validate re-checks every stored account against the service and takes whatever is in kaggle-inbox/ (kaggle.json or a `username token` line).
Only the accounts the team registry assigns to an owner are workers: one per person.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: validate the accounts and take the new credentials from the inbox.

actions.label: Remote rehearsal and launch (Kaggle / Colab)
guide: Order: generate-job → submit --smoke → fetch --smoke and smoke record → readiness → gate (operator only) → submit → status / poll → fetch.
The ledger is append-only; if the accounts do not authenticate, use /kaggle-accounts first.
Only the operator authorizes a launch: no agent runs submit on its own.
submit (--smoke too) requires that you validated the diagrams of the approved PoC and experiments.
actions.placeholder: E.g.: generate the job for experiments/e1.py and prepare its smoke rehearsal.

actions.desc: Products, verdicts and diagrams of the proof of concept and of the experiments.

sections.title: Materials And Methods
sections.principles: A rigorous, reproducible description without ambiguity. Formal models, mathematical formulation and system architecture.

canonical_blocks.question: What are the main modules and components of the system or model?
What base mechanisms or architectures are adopted and how do they connect?
What specific mathematical formulation or design is introduced?

sections.cross_relations: Specifies the architecture and methods whose performance the experimental sections evaluate.

sections.title: Experimental Setup
sections.principles: Reproducible validation protocols: bench/dataset setup, instrumentation, evaluation metrics and parameters.

canonical_blocks.question: What methodological strategy validates the proposal?
What data sources, instruments or test environments were used?
What are the success criteria and formal performance metrics?
What are the hyperparameters, rates and experimentation protocols?

sections.cross_relations: Fixes the empirical rules and conditions to evaluate the hypotheses stated in the Introduction.

sections.title: Results And Discussion
sections.principles: Density of quantitative evidence. Corroboration with plots, performance tables and contrast with baselines.

canonical_blocks.question: Are the main hypotheses stated in the introduction corroborated?
What empirical results were obtained against the success metrics?
What quantitative and qualitative advantages are shown over the state of the art?

sections.cross_relations: Empirically validates the stated hypotheses, confirming the Abstract's claims.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.principles: Constructive self-criticism and scientific honesty: assumptions, computational complexity, trade-offs and failure conditions.

canonical_blocks.question: What are the work's validity limits and assumptions?
What compute, energy or data requirements constrain the system?
What scenarios or distributions have not been covered exhaustively yet?
In which edge cases or under which perturbations could performance degrade?
How can these limitations be mitigated in future iterations?

sections.cross_relations: Engages with the Related Work and sets the priority lines for future work.

sections.title: Related Work
sections.principles: Rigorous comparative taxonomy against the state of the art (SOTA). A formal table contrasting key features, metrics and gaps.

canonical_blocks.question: How has the field evolved and what are its main strands?
What strengths and weaknesses do the relevant prior works show?
How do the existing limitations affect overall performance?
Why does the proposal stand apart from the SOTA?
How does the comparative analysis support the methodological decisions taken?

sections.cross_relations: Sets the frame of reference that justifies the design and experimentation decisions.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.principles: Sequential argument construction: problem justification, methodological map, current bottleneck, proposed solution, testable hypotheses and contributions.

canonical_blocks.question: What is the problem's context and fundamental motivation?
How were the research and its framework structured?
What technical or theoretical limitations prevent solving the problem today?
How does the proposed system address the identified limitations?
What hypotheses does the study put to an empirical test?
How is the reading of the following sections organized?
What are the article's definitive scientific and technical contributions?

sections.cross_relations: The stated hypotheses are validated one by one in Results and synthesized in Conclusions.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.principles: A conclusive synthesis of the fundamental contributions without repeating raw data. Outlook and directions for future work.

canonical_blocks.question: What fundamental challenge did this research take on and solve?
What are the main findings and consolidated advances?
What practical or theoretical implications does this advance have for the discipline?
What resources remain available to the community and what future work opens?

sections.cross_relations: Closes the argumentative cycle opened in the Abstract and the Introduction.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.principles: Canonical slot structure: Context -> Technical gap -> Methodological proposal -> Architecture/Design -> Experimental results -> Accuracy/Performance -> Impact and reproducibility.

canonical_blocks.question: Why does this problem matter and what is the application domain?
What shortcomings or limitations do current approaches have?
What does this work propose to close that gap?
What components make up the proposed system or model?
What performance metrics and empirical validation were reached?
What accuracy, latency or empirical advantage was shown?
How does this advance change the research field?

sections.cross_relations: Summarizes the whole manuscript; every slot anticipates a section of the paper.

sections.title: Title And Keywords
sections.principles: Informative technical concision without ambiguous acronyms. Identify the system/model and the application domain.

canonical_blocks.question: What is the work's technical contribution and application domain?
What are the manuscript's indexable terms and descriptors?

sections.cross_relations: Projects the key terms that the Abstract develops and the Introduction formalizes.

sections.title: Back Matter
sections.principles: Formal transparency: CRediT authorship, funding sources, data/code availability and ethics statements.

canonical_blocks.question: What roles and contributions did each author of the manuscript take on?
What projects, grants or bodies funded the research?
Where do the datasets, source code and reproducible artifacts live?
Is there any financial or personal conflict of interest to declare?
Which institutions, reviewers or technical collaborators are thanked?
What mathematical derivations, supplementary tables or details are appended?

sections.cross_relations: Meets the regulatory and ethical requirements of academic publishing.
